consensus_summary: Primary meaning across responses is a season or place of trial, suffering, grief, danger or spiritual low point/darkness through which God accompanies and sustains (driven by Ps 23:4, also Baca etc.). Common alternatives include humility/lowliness exalted by God (Isa 40:4), judgment/decision (Jehoshaphat/Hinnom), restoration from desolation (dry bones/Achor), and minority fruitfulness or pure geography. No single fixed symbol but strong popular convention for the trial reading.
book_summary: Valley is the low and humbled, opposite of the mountain-kingdom; every valley shall be exalted (Isa 40:4). Explicitly notes the common teaching is low seasons of trial and death set against the mountaintop.
consensus_core_identification: season/place of trial, suffering or spiritual low point
book_core_identification: the low and humbled (status/persons), opposite of the mountain-kingdom
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates the humility/lowliness motif (Isa 40:4) to the core identification and demotes the dominant trial/death-season motif (Ps 23) to mere common teaching; it therefore reclassifies experiential trial cases out of the primary symbolic extension while retaining the general category of low things that are raised, and links the low specifically to opposition against mountain-kingdoms.
material_contradiction: None; the two identifications can hold of different biblical contexts/senses and the book does not deny the trial reading.
rationale: Book core ('low and humbled') is already listed as a common alternative in every consensus response and is tied to the same Isa 40:4 text. It therefore preserves the general referent/category of valley-as-low while materially changing emphasis, boundary and primary extension—away from consensus trial seasons toward status humility opposite kingdoms. This is boundary/precision disagreement (REFINED), not core replacement (DIVERGENT) or absence from consensus (NOVEL). Cores overlap compatibly on lowliness that is exalted.
strongest_objection: The Ps 23 trial reading is so overwhelmingly dominant in preaching, hymnody and devotion that elevating the secondary Isa 40 humility motif constitutes a stronger replacement of the central identification than a mere refinement of boundaries.
